text:
Nashville has won seven straight, the last one a shootout against Vegas on Friday that Roman Josi finished, and the Predators sit at 11-4-5 with 27 points. Our playoff odds have them at 71%. That's a long way from where a lot of people expected this group to be, and the reason is mostly in the crease.

Juuse Saros has stopped 94.9% of shots over his last five starts, 7.2 goals better than an average goalie would have done with the same shots, and across the season Nashville has allowed 13.7 fewer goals than its chances against predicted. The skaters are roughly even: 49% of the expected goals overall, 47% at five on five. Our numbers think the Preds have about six more points than their play deserves.

The roster has a new piece in the middle. Shane Wright arrived from Seattle on November 1 for Matthew Wood, and Andrew Brunette wants him at center with pace; he had three points against Anaheim on Wednesday. Steven Stamkos has been in the headlines all week too, and the pairing of Josi and Adam Wilsby (57% of the expected goals) has been the best thing about the skating group.

What to watch is simple: whether the five-on-five play catches up to the goaltending before the goaltending cools. The Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix pair, at 43%, is where the chances leak.
headline: Saros is carrying a seven-game Preds run
